requirement: The `habeas-requirements` skill MUST direct agents to present each group to the user with its exact text, including any `{sites}` and `{violations}` queries, and with each design question the review returned, along with its options and the presenting agent's recommendation.
rationale:
The requirement has one obligation. The `habeas-requirements` skill must direct agents to present each group to the user with three things:
- the group's exact text, including any `{sites}` and `{violations}` queries;
- each design question the review returned;
- each question's options and the presenting agent's recommendation.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_requirements_skill_presents_exact_text_and_design_questions]` is marked `{test}` for the subject. It calls `assert_phrases("habeas-requirements", ...)`. That helper runs `assert_text` on `bundled_skill(name)`, which is the collapsed text of the skill's `SKILL.md` and reference files. Collapsing whitespace means the wrapped lines in the skill still match.

The phrase it requires is "Present each group to the user: its exact text, including any `{sites}` and `{violations}` queries, and the design questions the review returned, each with its options and your recommendation". This sentence states every element of the requirement: the exact text, both query kinds, the design questions, and their options and recommendation. I found that sentence in step 4 of the Workflow in `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md`. The assertion fails if any part of the directive is dropped or reworded, so it enforces the obligation.

This is a documentation-content requirement, so a phrase-presence check is the appropriate test. The skill has no branching behavior to exercise. Other tests, such as `the_requirements_skill_reviews_each_group_with_a_parallel_read_only_subagent`, check where this step falls in the workflow. That ordering is outside this requirement. I found no gaps.
